solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Foreign money originally only put in cash machine arbitrarily

indicators.note: the original, first letter of 'only'

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs foreign banknotes into a cashpoint without any system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in' reads as depositing cash, but it is the instruction to place letters inside the machine's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: done arbitrarily means done without plan or reason, by chance.

clue.text: Connected ideas with a cost to be refined

indicators.note: refining reworks the material, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters; 'with' just joins the two parts

explanation.surface: A business pitch where related ideas must be costed and polished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Connected ideas' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Connected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: linked people or things are said to be associated, as in associated companies.

clue.text: Go off rhubarb

definitions.meaning: what food does when it spoils

explanation.surface: A stick of rhubarb has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense, the same as rot; the surface makes it the vegetable going off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot as a verb is to decay, and as a noun it is nonsense.

clue.text: Ramen ingredients possibly in new bags

parts.note: bags of something = oodles, lots of it

explanation.surface: Someone buying fresh packets of ramen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like packaging but means a large quantity, as in 'bags of time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: ramen is a Japanese noodle soup, and 'possibly' allows for its other ingredients.

clue.text: Best change work on bogus imitations

indicators.note: bogus imitations are false, so the letters are not in their true order

explanation.surface: A plea to put the best face on a range of counterfeit goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description rather than a synonym, which is why it hides so well at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: optimising means changing something to make it the best it can be.

clue.text: Charm of American drinking vermouth cocktail

parts.note: mojo = a charm or magic power, an American usage
Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: An American's appeal as he sips a vermouth cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for Italian vermouth comes from the old British bar order 'gin and it'. 'Of American' marks mojo as an American word.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a Cuban drink of rum, lime, sugar and mint, one of the best-known cocktails.

clue.text: When taken up, a piece of plissé is enough for items of loungewear

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up reads the letters upward
the answer is a piece of the words that follow

parts.note: the run pliSSE IS ENOugh, accent dropped

explanation.surface: Sewing talk: a scrap of pleated fabric is enough for some pyjamas.
explanation.walkthrough: Plissé is a pleated fabric, so the surface sounds like dressmaking; the hidden run is read upward to give ONESIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: all-in-one zipped suits worn for lounging at home.

clue.text: Head of innovation weirdly not great in bringing elements together

indicators.note: the letters are arranged weirdly
the head is the first letter

parts.note: the letters of not great in, rearranged

explanation.surface: A head of innovation who is oddly poor at getting teams to work together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like the preposition but belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: to integrate is to combine separate parts into one whole.

clue.text: Somewhat momentous sign of things to come

indicators.note: only some of the word is used

explanation.surface: Something momentous is foreshadowed.
explanation.walkthrough: The hiding place is a single word, and 'momentous' fits the surface's air of portent.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a portent, an event read as foretelling the future.

clue.text: Leave, or keep being swamped by inflexible hours

parts.note: a keep is a castle stronghold

explanation.surface: A choice between quitting and staying on under rigid working hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb opposed to 'Leave', but it is the noun: a castle's keep.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to set out or depart on a journey.

clue.text: Courage of outspoken copper?

indicators.note: spoken out, so it is the sound that counts

explanation.surface: The bravery of a blunt police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper is British slang for a police officer, which the surface leans on; here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: spirit or pluck, as in 'show your mettle'.

clue.text: The eastern side of Suwałki in Poland is a crumbling urban area

indicators.note: the letters crumble into a new order
east is the right-hand side, the last letter

parts.note: the letters of in Poland is a, rearranged

explanation.surface: A travel note about a run-down district of the Polish town of Suwałki.
explanation.walkthrough: The Polish setting steers away from America; Suwałki only supplies its final I.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the capital city of the US state of Indiana.

clue.text: Making remarks about place, one is flattering

indicators.note: the remarks go about, around, the other letters

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: Someone praising a location while remarking on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making remarks about place' reads as describing a location; 'about' is really the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: praising someone, paying them compliments.

clue.text: Designations held by Anna and Bonnie?

definitions.text: Designations held by Anna and Bonnie?

parts.note: surface reading: titles or names given to people; setter's reading: N, the abbreviation for name
surface reading: names two women carry; setter's reading: the letters NN sit at the very centre of both ANNA and BONNIE

explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name, so the NN held at the centre of both Anna and Bonnie is literally their middle names.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle names are the designations people hold between first name and surname.

clue.text: Serious nature of cut close to the head

indicators.note: the close, the end, of 'the'

explanation.surface: A grim remark about a haircut done right against the scalp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to the head' reads as a short haircut; 'close to the' actually gives E and a head is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the quality of being grave, stern or harsh.

clue.text: Key, fateful day for White House staffers?

parts.note: the Ides of March, when Caesar was killed

explanation.surface: A crucial, doom-laden day for the President's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as an adjective meaning crucial; it is the musical key of A.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: presidential assistants are the best-known staffers called by this name.

clue.text: Neat, and with a bow?

definitions.meaning: a bow is the front of a vessel, so read literally: shaped like one

explanation.surface: A neatly tied parcel finished with a ribbon bow.
explanation.walkthrough: The bow is the front of a ship, not a ribbon; the question mark flags reading SHIPSHAPE literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means tidy, and taken literally it means having a ship's form, bow included.

clue.text: Instruct employees to start late and become more cheerful

indicators.note: MEN starts late, missing its first letter

explanation.surface: A manager telling staff to come in late to lift morale.
explanation.walkthrough: Men is a crossword stock term for employees or workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to inform or educate someone.

clue.text: Nerve centres in trouble over supporting group of criminals

indicators.note: in a down clue, over turns the word upward

explanation.surface: The masterminds of a criminal ring are in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nerve centres' looks like a gang's headquarters but is anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomical sense: clusters of nerve cells that act as relay centres in the nervous system.

clue.text: Completely gave up booze in the end

indicators.note: only the end of 'booze' is taken

explanation.surface: Someone who eventually stopped drinking entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' reads as 'eventually'; it takes only the final letter of booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: in 'quite right' or 'not quite finished' the word means completely.

clue.text: Analgesic substance — one of five in recreational drug

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: A painkiller identified as one ingredient of a street drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like the connector but is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a bark alkaloid used against fever and pain.

clue.text: Northern police upset with conman refusing to be arrested, say

indicators.note: police and conman are upset, jumbled together

parts.note: the letters of police and conman, rearranged

explanation.surface: Northern officers are annoyed at a swindler who resisted arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks resisting arrest as just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: resisting arrest is one way of failing to obey an order.

clue.text: Ace female academic

parts.note: an ace is an expert, a pro

explanation.surface: Praise for a brilliant woman scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' reads as an adjective praising the academic; it is the noun, an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal abbreviation: short for professor, a senior university teacher.

clue.text: Discover the truth about fight in West Side Story?

definitions.meaning: British slang for seeing through someone
the Jets and Sharks arrange a gang fight

explanation.surface: Uncovering the real story of the gang fight in the musical.
explanation.walkthrough: To rumble someone is British slang for finding them out. The question mark marks the musical's fight as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumble means both to see through someone's deception and a street gang fight, the musical's word for it.

clue.text: League sport needing no introduction

indicators.note: the introduction, the first letter, is dropped

parts.note: DALLIANCE, amorous sport, without its first letter D

explanation.surface: A sports league so famous it needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is not a game here but dalliance, playful flirtation.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a union of parties for a common purpose, as in the League of Nations.

clue.text: What lepidopterist may use in depth every so often

indicators.note: letters are taken at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A butterfly collector working thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: A lepidopterist studies butterflies and moths.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: butterfly collectors catch specimens with a fine mesh on a pole.

clue.text: Monetary fine is mostly collected

indicators.note: most of the word, all but its last letter

parts.note: CALM = collected, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A remark that most of a financial penalty has been paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' reads as a monetary penalty, matching 'Monetary', but it is just the letter F; 'collected' means calm, not gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: relating to money, especially government revenue.

clue.text: Answer appeal to get hold of superlative building material

parts.note: an SOS is a distress appeal

explanation.surface: A plea to track down top-quality construction supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superlative' is both a grammar term and praise; either way it gives BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a fibrous mineral once widely used for insulation and fireproofing in buildings.
